questions.q: An image is 800 pixels wide and 600 pixels high, with a colour depth of 8 bits. Calculate its file size in bits.
questions.feedback: File size = width × height × colour depth = 800 × 600 × 8.
questions.hint: Work out how many pixels there are first, then how many bits each one needs.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 7 — Capacity calculator, station 2: Image file size

questions.q: An image is 1,000 × 500 pixels with a colour depth of 24 bits. Calculate its file size in megabytes.

methodMark.label: works out the size in bits (12,000,000)
converts to bytes by dividing by 8 (1,500,000)

questions.feedback: 1,000 × 500 × 24 = 12,000,000 bits; ÷ 8 = 1,500,000 bytes; ÷ 1,000 twice = 1.5 MB. Each step earns its own mark.
questions.hint: Bits first, then bytes, then up through the units.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 7 — Capacity calculator, station 2: Image file size

questions.q: Explain what happens to the file size of an image when its colour depth is doubled from 8 bits to 16 bits.

markPoints.concept: because every pixel now needs twice as many bits
accept: every pixel|each pixel|per pixel|every point|each point|each one|every one
markPoints.exemplar: This is because each pixel now needs twice as many bits.

questions.example: The file size doubles, because the number of pixels has not changed but each one now needs sixteen bits instead of eight.
questions.paraphrase: It becomes twice as big, since every single pixel is stored in twice as much space as before.
questions.feedback: The size, then the reason. The reason is that colour depth is per pixel.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 7 — Capacity calculator, station 2: Image file size

questions.q: A sound file is recorded at a sample rate of 44,100 Hz, with a bit depth of 16 bits, for 30 seconds. Calculate its file size in bits.
questions.feedback: File size = sample rate × bit depth × duration.
questions.hint: How many samples a second, how many bits a sample, and for how long?
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 7 — Capacity calculator, station 3: Sound file size

questions.q: A 10-second recording is sampled 8,000 times a second with a bit depth of 8. Calculate its file size in kilobytes.

methodMark.label: works out the size in bits (640,000)
converts to bytes by dividing by 8 (80,000)

questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 7 — Capacity calculator, station 3: Sound file size

questions.q: A plain text file contains 2,400 characters, each stored in 8 bits. Calculate its file size in bytes.
questions.feedback: Each character is one byte, so 2,400 characters is 2,400 bytes.
questions.hint: How many bits is each character, and how many bytes is that?
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 7 — Capacity calculator, station 4: Text file size

questions.q: A pupil says a Word document with 2,400 characters in it will be exactly 2,400 bytes. Explain why it will actually be larger.

markPoints.concept: the file also stores formatting and other information about the document
markPoints.exemplar: The file also stores formatting information such as fonts and styles.

markPoints.concept: so the file is larger than the characters alone
markPoints.exemplar: This means the file is bigger than the characters on their own.

questions.example: A Word document stores more than the characters: it also stores formatting such as fonts, sizes and colours, along with other metadata, so the file is bigger than the text alone.
questions.paraphrase: There is extra information in it besides the letters — how they are styled and laid out — which makes it larger.
questions.feedback: The calculation is for the characters. A real document file has more in it than that.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 7 — Capacity calculator, station 4: Text file size
